summary: Forest Service lookout near Georgetown Lake; 1937 press describes construction (Kamstra gives 1934); staffed to 1943; reported destroyed or removed; site today not described.

facts.design: 20-foot log tower with a frame cab; 14-foot-square tower and living quarters per 1937 press; called a 20-foot pole L-4 tower by Kamstra
facts.status_note: Kamstra says destroyed in 1978; Kemnow says removed, no date; firelookout.org lists it as gone

events.note: Construction begun June 1937 (newspaper dated June 24, 1937) and tower completed and accepted by early September 1937 (newspaper dated September 3, 1937), per Butte and Anaconda newspapers quoted on Kemnow's page; Kamstra gives 1934
A lookout observer took over the tower after it was accepted in September 1937
Lightning destroyed a tree near the lookout (newspaper dated June 24, 1938); the forest supervisor, Charles A. Joy, said the lookout was not damaged
Newspaper dated September 28, 1939 reports John Ringdahl would be taken off the post as the last observer; his removal would mark the official close of the 1939 fire season
Newspaper dated June 29, 1940: lookout was the only one in its district; Ancient Order of Squirrels membership cards to be issued there by Carl Ermelbauer
Newspaper dated July 20, 1943: Anna Beth Glaser named the first woman lookout in the Deer Lodge National Forest and appointed to serve atop Cable Mountain
Kamstra's page gives destroyed 1978; Kemnow's page says removed without a date

evidence.supports: lookout construction begun June 1937 on Cable Mountain northeast of Georgetown Lake
evidence.quote: June 24, 1937: Construction of a fire lookout on Cable mountain northeast of Georgetown lake was begun this week by the U.S. Forestry service

evidence.supports: frame building on a 20-foot log tower
evidence.quote: The lookout will be a frame building on a 20-foot log tower.

evidence.supports: telephone line to be strung and trail to be blazed to the lookout
evidence.quote: A telephone line will be strung and a trail will be blazed to the lookout.

evidence.supports: temporary camp served as the lookout in summer 1937
evidence.quote: A temporary camp there now serves as a lookout.

evidence.supports: tower started in early August 1937
evidence.quote: The 14-foot-square tower and living quarters was started early in August.

evidence.supports: completed and accepted in early September 1937
evidence.quote: September 3, 1937: Cable mountain lookout northeast of Georgetown was completed and accepted by the U,S. Forestry service yesterday

evidence.supports: Kamstra dates the tower 1934 and calls it a 20-foot pole L-4 tower; destroyed 1978
evidence.quote: 1934: 20' pole L-4 tower. Destroyed 1978.

evidence.supports: a lookout observer took over the tower at completion in September 1937
evidence.quote: A lookout station in a temporary tent camp during the summer took over his duties at the tower yesterday.

evidence.supports: late September 1939: Ringdahl to be taken off the post; removal to mark the close of the 1939 season
evidence.quote: September 28, 1939: The last lookout observer to be taken from his post in the Deer Lodge National Forest this season will leave his station at the Cable mountain lookout Saturday

evidence.supports: John Ringdahl named; his removal to mark the official close of the 1939 fire season
evidence.quote: He is John Ringdahl, and his removal will mark the official close of the 1939 fire season in this forest.

evidence.supports: 1940 membership cards for the Ancient Order of Squirrels
evidence.quote: June 29, 1940: Membership cards to the Ancient Order of Squirrels have been received in Anaconda

evidence.supports: in 1940 the lookout was the only one in its district
evidence.quote: The lookout is the only one at present in this district.

evidence.supports: membership granted to those climbing to the lookout
evidence.quote: Membership is granted to those climbing to the lookout and promising to exercise caution in the forest.

evidence.supports: Carl Ermelbauer to issue the cards at the lookout
evidence.quote: where Carl Ermelbauer will issue them to any individual climbing to the lookout tower at that site.

evidence.supports: Anna Beth Glaser named first woman lookout in the Deer Lodge National Forest in July 1943
evidence.quote: July 20, 1943: Miss Anna Beth Glaser, 19, Anaconda, Monday was named the first woman lookout in the Deer Lodge National Forest's history.

evidence.supports: Glaser appointed to serve atop Cable Mountain
evidence.quote: District Ranger Eric P. White appointed the Montana State college co-ed to serve atop Cable Mountain

evidence.supports: June 1938: lightning destroyed a tree near the lookout; forest supervisor Charles A. Joy
evidence.quote: June 24, 1938: Lightning destroyed a tree near Cable Mountain lookout during recent storms, Charles A. Joy, supervisor of the Deer Lodge national forest, stated yesterday

evidence.supports: the lookout itself was not damaged
evidence.quote: He said the forest service lookout was not damaged.

evidence.supports: Kemnow lists the tower as removed, with no date
evidence.quote: Removed

evidence.supports: firelookout.org lists the tower as gone
evidence.quote: Cable Mountain Deer Lodge 46.21766 -113.22130 Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kamstra gives 1934. The Butte and Anaconda newspaper reports quoted on Kemnow's page describe construction beginning in June 1937 and acceptance in early September 1937. The story follows the 1937 reports.

notes_for_editor: Built year conflicts: Kamstra 1934 vs 1937 press (story follows press). Fate conflicts: destroyed 1978 (Kamstra) vs removed, undated (Kemnow). Location conflict in the record remains open: FFLA 46.21766,-113.2213 vs west_us_lookouts 46.2527,-113.19339, about 4.4 km apart; the 1937 papers only say northeast of Georgetown Lake. Last known staffing is 1943; no later date found. Not checked: the forest's current name, and whether anything remains on the peak.
